newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS PLAYS DOWN SPLIT TALK.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS PLAYS DOWN SPLIT TALK.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Thursday played down market talk of a possible split-up of the company, reiterating that it was pursuing its previously announced process of evaluating units and preparing budgets for its businesses.
Cor Boonstra, chairing his first annual results news conference since taking over as Philips chairman last October, declined to be drawn on concrete strategy moves.
"We're exactly on line with what we stated," he said when pressed for strategy details. "We stick to our timetable," he told journalists.

Boonstra reiterated Philips' plan of weeding out underperformers, setting budgets for its units and making units more accountable for themselves and said the company was looking at long-term strategy but would not reveal its plans for some time.
"At the end of this year, beginning of 1998 we will come up with a report about the strategy we've decided on," he told a news conference to present Philips' 1996 figures.
He said the relationship with 75 percent owned music and films group PolyGram NV was not under review, tackling speculation the unit would be put up for sale.

He reiterated Philips' commitment to its troubled Sound and Vision unit, which makes televisions and audio equipment, saying: "There's not a serious consideration, there's not even an unserious consideration, to change our relationship with Sound and Vision."

Industry watchers and some analysts have speculated that Boonstra might be tempted to fulfil his target of maximising value to Philips shareholders by splitting up the company and going forward in a drastically pared down format. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31-20-504-5014
